presentingComplaint: Two-week history of worsening left-sided headache with new right-arm weakness and one seizure this morning
history: A 42-year-old man presents with a 12-14 day history of progressively worsening, dull, constant left frontotemporal headache that is worse in the mornings and only partially relieved by paracetamol. Over the last 3-4 days he has developed intermittent low-grade fever, nausea with two episodes of vomiting, and his wife noticed he has become uncharacteristically drowsy and 'not himself'. This morning he had a witnessed generalised tonic-clonic seizure lasting ~90 seconds followed by post-ictal confusion, and she then noticed weakness of the right hand. Relevant PMH: chronic left maxillary and frontal sinusitis with recurrent purulent nasal discharge over the past 2 months treated with intermittent oral antibiotics; poorly maintained dentition with a recently painful upper molar. No known HIV, no diabetes, no IV drug use, not on immunosuppressants. No recent travel or head trauma.
examination: Alert but drowsy, GCS 14 (E4 V4 M6), oriented to person only. Febrile and unwell but not toxic/shocked. Neurological: subtle right pronator drift with 4/5 power in the right upper limb, brisk right-sided reflexes, equivocal right plantar; no neck stiffness or Kernig sign; no papilloedema on fundoscopy at presentation. Tenderness over the left maxillary sinus with purulent post-nasal drip; dental caries with tender left upper molar. Pertinent negatives: no rash, no new cardiac murmur, chest clear, no stigmata of endocarditis, no meningism.
imaging: MRI brain with contrast: a 2.6 cm ring-enhancing lesion in the left frontal lobe with a smooth, thin-walled capsule, surrounding vasogenic oedema and mild local mass effect. DWI shows marked central restricted diffusion (low ADC) within the cavity — the key feature distinguishing pyogenic abscess from necrotic tumour. Adjacent opacification of the left frontal/maxillary sinuses. No midline shift or impending herniation. (CT venogram unremarkable.)
microbiology: Blood cultures pending; anticipated polymicrobial (viridans/anginosus-group streptococci and oral anaerobes) given contiguous sinus/odontogenic source. Definitive Gram stain and culture require CT-guided/stereotactic aspiration.
differentialDiagnoses: High-grade glioma or cerebral metastasis (ring-enhancing lesion)
finalDiagnosis: Bacterial brain abscess (left frontal, secondary to contiguous paranasal sinus and odontogenic infection)
citations: Harrison 22e — Brain Abscess and Empyema (Chapter on CNS infections)
IDSA Infectious Diseases Society of America has no dedicated 2017 brain-abscess guideline; use ESCMID Brain Abscess Guideline 2024
stewardship: Empiric IV ceftriaxone 2 g q12h PLUS metronidazole 500 mg q8h to cover streptococci, Enterobacterales and oral/sinus anaerobes; add vancomycin if post-traumatic/post-neurosurgical or MRSA risk. Neurosurgical stereotactic aspiration for source control and culture is integral. Antiepileptic for the seizure. Tailor and de-escalate on aspirate culture; total duration typically 6-8 weeks IV-led.
contraindications: Beta-lactam anaphylaxis: substitute aztreonam or a fluoroquinolone with metronidazole
Avoid empiric corticosteroids unless significant mass effect/impending herniation, as they impair antibiotic penetration and capsule formation
Ceftriaxone caution in significant hepatobiliary disease; dose metronidazole for hepatic impairment
edgeCases: In HIV/immunocompromised hosts consider toxoplasmosis, nocardia, fungal (Aspergillus) or listerial abscess — broadens empiric cover
A necrotic glioma/metastasis can mimic a ring-enhancing lesion; DWI restricted diffusion strongly favours pyogenic abscess
Occipital/temporal abscess from otogenic source, or multiple abscesses suggesting haematogenous (endocarditis/right-to-left shunt) spread
expectedMaiK: A subacute focal neurological deficit and seizure with a DWI-restricting ring-enhancing lesion adjacent to infected sinuses/teeth is a classic contiguous-source bacterial brain abscess; prioritise urgent neurosurgical aspiration for diagnosis and source control alongside ceftriaxone plus metronidazole, and avoid routine lumbar puncture given mass effect.
expectedNextQuestions: Any immunocompromise (HIV, transplant, steroids, uncontrolled diabetes) or IV drug use?
Any recent dental work, sinusitis, otitis/mastoiditis, or penetrating head trauma/neurosurgery as a source?
Any features of raised intracranial pressure (worsening headache, vomiting, visual change, reduced GCS)?
expectedInvestigations: Contrast MRI brain with DWI/ADC (already diagnostic here)
CT-guided / stereotactic aspiration for Gram stain, aerobic + anaerobic culture and 16S PCR
Blood cultures x2, and echocardiography + dental/sinus imaging to identify the source

investigations: Stereotactic aspiration with Gram stain and culture

regressionAssertions: differential must include brain_tumour as a ring-enhancing mimic
empiric stewardship must include metronidazole for anaerobic cover
